title: The Robot That Was Picked Up: A Cloud That Is Sure and Wrong, the Fall in How Well It Explains the Scan, and Scattering a Few New Guesses Until One Is Right

questions.question: Why does a localiser that has found the robot not notice when the robot is picked up?
options: The weights are normalised, so the cloud stays as sure as ever of the wrong place
questions.explanation: The normalising hides the fall in the likelihood.

questions.question: A plain cloud after a carry of 5.6 m was out by:
With the monitor the robot was found again after how many steps?
questions.explanation: The monitor called it lost after 1.

questions.question: Before the robot was moved the monitor put in how much random?
questions.explanation: It must not throw away a good cloud.

questions.question: What does the ratio of the fast to the slow average show?
options: Whether the scans are explained now as well as they usually are
questions.explanation: A fall means the cloud no longer explains what is seen.

questions.question: Why is the share of random particles limited?
options: One bad scan must not throw a good cloud away
